paras: The lynching of Minor Long was the killing of a Black prisoner by masked men inside the parish jail at St. Francisville, Louisiana, on the night of October 5 or 6, 1903. After taking the keys from the jailer, the men shot Long to death in his cell when a rope they had called for did not arrive. A New York Sun dispatch about the killing was reprinted under the headline "Lynching Outrage" and condensed in rural and German-language papers.

Long had been held in the parish jail for about a week. According to the Sun's dispatch, he "was accused of shooting at a white man more than a year ago." He was confined in a steel cage with two other Black prisoners.

At night "a handful of masked men" came to the jail and demanded the jailer's keys. When he refused, they ordered him to lie still and took the keys from him; a German-language version said he was thrown to the ground. The men then went to the cage where Long was held.

Their leader called to one of his followers to bring a rope, and when it did not come at once he ordered "a general fire on the helpless prisoner." Within seconds Long was "literally riddled with bullets," and the men "quietly dispersed."
None of the reports names the attackers, the jailer or the other prisoners, and no report of an arrest, inquest or grand jury inquiry appears in the coverage.

The story reached print as a special dispatch to the New York Sun, which ran it on October 7 under the headline "Shot to Death in Jail" with the subhead "Negro Killed in the Cells Because a Rope Was Not at Hand." The Minneapolis Journal printed the same text that day as "New York Sun Special Service" under the headline "Lynching Outrage," and the Marshalltown, Iowa, Evening Times-Republican repeated it on October 8. Both kept the wire's description of Long as "the helpless prisoner" while repeating the charge against him.

Later condensations hardened the accusation into fact. The Sharp County Record of Arkansas, in a column of general news, described Long as "a negro who attempted to murder a white man" who was "taken from jail" and riddled with bullets. At the end of October the German-language Nebraska Staats-Anzeiger und Herold ran the item as "Im Gefängnisse gelyncht" (lynched in jail), calling the attackers "der Mob" and stating that Long had shot a white man about a year before; the Milwaukee Vorwärts printed the same brief on November 1.

The date depends on the printing: the Sun's dispatch, dated October 6, placed the attack "last night," while reprints with October 7 and October 8 datelines said "last night" and "Tuesday night," pointing to October 6. Because the reprints carry the Sun's text under their own datelines, the Sun's original is the better guide to the date. The briefs also differ from the wire on where Long died, saying he was taken from his cell or from the jail, whereas the fuller Sun account has him shot inside the cage.

reader.title: Lynching of Minor Long
bases: Masked men seized the jail keys and shot a Black prisoner to death in his cell after calling for a rope, which the headlines called a 'Lynching Outrage' and the German press 'gelyncht' (A1, A2, A5).

A 'handful of masked men' with a leader and 'followers' overpowered the jailer and shot Long dead in the parish jail with no lawful authority (A1, A2). The papers tie the killing to an accusation that he had shot at a white man more than a year earlier, and the leader first called for a rope, the form of a punitive hanging (A1, A2, A4).

Every English account is the same New York Sun dispatch (A1) reprinted or condensed (A2, A3, A4), and the German brief (A5, A6) follows its details; no local Louisiana report, Black-press account or independent follow-up was found.

accounts.label: New York Sun wire report
accounts.gist: Masked men took the jailer's keys, went to the steel cage holding Long and two others, and, lacking a rope, shot Long to death; he was accused of shooting at a white man more than a year before.

accounts.label: German-language brief
accounts.gist: Several masked men threw the jailer down and took the key; the mob took Long from his cell and, with no rope at hand, shot him in the jail; it says Long had shot a white man about a year earlier.

accounts.label: Arkansas news digest
accounts.gist: Long, 'a negro who attempted to murder a white man', was taken from jail 'one day last week' and riddled with bullets.

framing.detail: The Sun's wire calls Long 'the helpless prisoner' and reprints headlined it 'Lynching Outrage', while still giving the accusation against him.
The Sharp County Record listed the killing among unrelated items and stated as fact that Long 'attempted to murder a white man'.
German-language weeklies ran a brief headed 'Im Gefängnisse gelyncht' (lynched in jail) that called the attackers 'der Mob' and stated that Long had shot a white man.
